title: pvglTFReader
body:
## pvglTFReader

Reads a glTF 2.0 asset (.gltf with external buffers, or binary .glb) into a multiblock dataset of polydata for one scene, with skinning, morph targets and enabled animations applied to the geometry when ApplyDeformationsToGeometry is true. Animations become time steps sampled at Framerate. Materials and textures are not applied. Use it to bring 3-D models or animated scenes into a pipeline; for static CAD surfaces pvWavefrontOBJReader or readSTL are simpler.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- No animation is enabled by default (glTF does not define which should play); list them in AnimationStatus to get time steps.
- glTF coordinates are metres by specification, but scenes from other tools may not follow that; nothing is converted.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so inspect the output blocks, arrays and time steps on your own files before relying on it.

Native constructor: `glTFReader`. Identity: `sources/glTF 2.0 Reader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AnimationStatus` | Select the animations to enable. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `ApplyDeformationsToGeometry` | When true, skinning, morph-target and animation transforms are applied to the output point coordinates, so the geometry is posed for the current frame; false leaves the geometry undeformed and stores the transforms in field data. ParaView shows AnimationStatus and Framerate only when this is true. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `FileName` | Path of the .gltf or .glb file (glTF 2.0 only). A .gltf file refers to its .bin buffers and images by relative URI, so they must stay beside it; .glb embeds them. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; the value is passed when the node is created and must be a constant. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Framerate` | Sampling rate used to turn enabled animations into discrete time steps: steps run from 0 to the longest enabled animation's duration every 1/Framerate seconds, plus the final instant. 0 publishes only a time range without steps. It matters only when an animation is enabled. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `Scene` | Name of the glTF scene to read when the file defines several. Names are the file's scene names made unique (unnamed scenes become Unnamed, duplicates get _1, _2 suffixes); an unknown name makes vtkGLTFReader warn and keep its current scene. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvglTFReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
